_meta.indication: EMPAVELI is a complement inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study APL2-302 (also referred to as APL-302)
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, prospective randomized, multicenter, open-label, active comparator-controlled study; 80 adult subjects randomized 1:1 to pegcetacoplan 1,080 mg SC twice weekly or their current dose of eculizumab, with a 4-week run-in, 16-week randomized controlled period, and 32-week open-label period
pivotal_trials.population: C5 inhibitor (eculizumab)-experienced adult subjects with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change from baseline (CFB) in hemoglobin level at Week 16
pivotal_trials.n: N=80 adults randomized 1:1 (pegcetacoplan n=41, eculizumab n=39)
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant primary endpoint: adjusted LSM CFB in Hb was 2.4 g/dL (pegcetacoplan) vs -1.5 g/dL (eculizumab), mean difference 3.8 g/dL (95% CI 2.33 to 5.34) at Week 16, p<0.0001. Pegcetacoplan was noninferior for transfusion avoidance: 35 (85%) vs 6 (15%), treatment difference 63 (95% CI 48 to 77). Noninferiority was not met for CFB in LDH.

nct_ctgov.title: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of APL-2 in Patients With Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria (PNH)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥10%): injection-site reactions, infections, diarrhea, abdominal pain, respiratory tract infection, viral infection, and fatigue. In Study APL2-302: injection-site reaction 39% vs 5%, infections 29% vs 26%, diarrhea 22% vs 3%, respiratory tract infection 15% vs 13%, viral infection 12% vs 8%. Serious adverse events occurred in 7 (17%); most common serious reaction was infections (5%). Key risk is serious infections caused by encapsulated bacteria.
target_moa: Pegcetacoplan binds to complement protein C3 and its activation fragment C3b, regulating cleavage of C3 and generation of downstream complement effectors; it acts proximally in the complement cascade controlling both C3b-mediated extravascular hemolysis and terminal complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS INFECTIONS CAUSED BY ENCAPSULATED BACTERIA. Meningococcal infections may occur and may become rapidly life-threatening or fatal; EMPAVELI may predispose to serious infections, especially those caused by encapsulated bacteria such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis types A, C, W, Y, and B, and Haemophilus influenzae type B.

rems.type: EMPAVELI is available only through a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS); prescribers must enroll in the program to mitigate the risk of serious infections caused by encapsulated bacteria

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug

description.text: Added indication for treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with C3 glomerulopathy (C3G) or primary immune-complex membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (IC-MPGN) to reduce proteinuria

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the use of Empaveli (pegcetacoplan) for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with C3 glomerulopathy (C3G) or primary immune-complex membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (IC-MPGN), to reduce proteinuria, and proposed modification to the approved Empaveli REMS.

basis.text: Fast Track designation granted December 15, 2016 for patients with PNH who continue to experience hemolysis requiring RBC transfusions despite eculizumab; an additional Fast Track designation granted February 8, 2019 for the investigation of APL-2 for the treatment of PNH

citations.quote: The Applicant submitted a Fast Track designation request for APL-2 on October 14, 2016, for the treatment of patients with PNH who continue to experience hemolysis and as a result require RBC transfusions despite receiving therapy with eculizumab. Fast Track designation was granted on December 15, 2016.

An additional Fast Track designation request was submitted on December 10, 2018, proposing to broaden the indication of APL-2 for the treatment of all patients with PNH. This Fast Track designation request was granted on February 8, 2019, for the investigation of APL-2 for the treatment of PNH.

summary.text: Empaveli (pegcetacoplan) was submitted as an original NDA received 9/14/2020 and reviewed under Priority review. The product held Orphan Drug designation for PNH (granted April 20, 2014) and Fast Track designation (granted December 15, 2016 and again February 8, 2019). It was approved first cycle based on Phase 3 Study APL2-302; no accelerated approval or advisory committee was involved, and a REMS was required for the risk of serious encapsulated-bacteria infections.

requirement.text: 4047-1: Establish a registry to characterize the long-term safety of pegcetacoplan in adult PNH patients, including treatment-naive patients, with at least 5 years of follow-up, including development/worsening of autoimmune diseases and serious encapsulated-bacteria infections

citations.quote: 4047-1 Establish a registry to characterize the long-term safety of pegcetacoplan in adult patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), including patients who are treatment naïve, with at least 5 years of follow-up. Submit yearly safety follow-up data and a summary of the major safety findings for all patients, including the development or worsening of autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and all serious infections with encapsulated bacteria. The final study report should include an integrated safety dataset and patient level data, including data on pegcetacoplan dosing, meningococcal and pneumococcal vaccination status, and concomitant medications.
